ideation.icp_description: Brands that sell on Amazon (or are clearly building toward it), surfaced by the fact they are hiring for an Amazon / e-commerce / marketplace / DTC role. Company size 10-1,000 employees, HQ in North America or high-GDP Europe (US, CA, GB, IE, DE, NL, CH, SE, NO, DK, FI). Direct employers only (not recruiters). NOT Amazon agencies/consultancies (they are competitors), NOT brand aggregators/roll-ups, NOT AWS/cloud technical roles.
ideation.offer: Amplifyy is an Amazon growth agency. They grow a brand's Amazon sales (listings, Amazon advertising / PPC, account management, strategy) and stop climbing PPC spend bleeding into unprofitable growth. Navreo runs the cold outreach for Amplifyy and books discovery calls. Proven proof points: helped brands like Coleman and Yamaha scale to six figures a month on Amazon; Coleman to over $4M a month. Discovery-call incentive: $25 Amazon gift card regardless of fit. Soft CTA: free 15-minute screen-share teardown of one of the brand's Amazon listings.
ideation.why_signal_fits: A company hiring for an Amazon or e-commerce role is actively investing in that channel right now. Either they have a gap to fill (an agency like Amplifyy can be faster and lower-risk than waiting months for a full-time hire to ramp) or they are scaling the channel (and want expert execution on listings + PPC while the new hire focuses on strategy). Either way it is a warm moment to reach out.

qualification._purpose: Role-only judgement layer applied by lilly-theirstack-data-processing Phase 2.5. Classifies each new Jobs row as QUALIFIED / BORDERLINE / OFF_BRIEF based on whether the role signals 'a brand investing in its own Amazon / e-commerce selling channel'. Companies are NEVER excluded by this gate on industry/type alone — but note this signal's noise is dominated by look-alike ROLES (AWS engineers, agency-team roles, aggregator M&A roles, logistics) that share keywords without being a brand-side channel owner, and those roles ARE disqualified.
qualification.role_signal_definition: The new hire will own, build, or strongly influence the company's Amazon / marketplace / e-commerce SELLING operation (the channel through which the brand sells its own products to consumers). NOT a logistics/warehouse/fulfilment role, NOT a software engineer building on Amazon Web Services, NOT an agency/consultancy team member who sells Amazon services to others (a competitor), NOT an M&A/investment role at a brand aggregator.
qualified_role_patterns: Head of / VP / Director of Amazon (incl. Amazon Strategy / Growth / Vendor / Marketplace)
Amazon Brand / Channel / Account / Marketing / Advertising / Ads / PPC / Operations / Growth Manager (brand-side, selling own products)
Head of / VP / Director of E-commerce / Ecommerce; E-commerce Manager / Director (description confirms Amazon)
Head of / VP / Director of Marketplace(s); Marketplace Manager / Director
Head of / VP / Director of D2C / DTC; DTC Manager
Head of / Director of Online Sales; Online Sales Manager
Senior Amazon & Retail Media Manager; eCommerce Key Accounts Manager (brand-side)
disqualified_role_patterns: AWS / Amazon Web Services / Amazon Bedrock / Cloud / Software / Backend / Frontend Engineer / Developer — technical roles on Amazon's cloud, unrelated to selling products
Warehouse / Logistics / Fulfilment / Fulfillment / Supply Chain / Driver / Picker / Packer / Delivery / Amazon Flex — operations/logistics, not a channel-growth decision-maker
Cold Caller / Sales Setter / Appointment Setter / Inbound Sales Qualifier / SDR / BDR — junior sales, usually at an Amazon agency (a competitor)
Amazon / E-commerce Strategieberater / Berater / Consultant — agency/consultancy team member selling Amazon services to others (competitor, not a brand)
Deal Execution / M&A / Investment / Acquisition (E-commerce) — brand aggregator / roll-up buying Amazon businesses, not a brand growing its own channel
Intern / Working Student / Werkstudent / Praktikum / Graduate / Apprentice / Part-Time Student — no decision authority
Customer Service / Customer Support / Seller Support — support layer, not channel owner
borderline_role_patterns: Account Manager (E-commerce / Marketplaces) — could be a brand's internal e-comm AM OR an agency's client-facing AM; check the company is a brand
Supply Chain / Operations Manager (E-commerce) — leans logistics, but at a small brand may be the de-facto channel owner
Content / Content Operations Manager (E-commerce) — content-leaning; qualifies only if they own listings / the channel
Any role at a company that looks like an agency or consultancy despite a clean title — check it is an actual brand that sells its own products on Amazon
Sales Director of E-commerce Channels / eCommerce Key Accounts — channel-sales leaning; qualifies if brand-side

filter._expected_daily_volume: ~16 jobs/day, ~12 companies/day (30-day blurred test: 487 jobs / 367 companies with floor=10). Title-only would be ~41/day; the 'Amazon in description' filter cuts ~52% non-Amazon e-comm noise.
filter._filter_design_note: Title list AND description-contains-Amazon are ANDed in a single search. The description filter is the 'clever bit' that lets broad titles (Head of E-commerce, Head of DTC, etc.) through ONLY when the post actually mentions Amazon. job_description_pattern_or is the verified-working TheirStack API field for the live preview/dry-run (the live UI uses the Job Description 'contains any of' chip = 'Amazon').

dm_finder._note: Target the senior e-commerce decision-maker, NOT founders/CEOs by default (earlier Amplifyy outreach skewed to founders, who were the wrong buyer). For a very small brand with no e-commerce lead, find the most senior person available (e.g. Founder/Owner) as a fallback. Skip 'Account Manager' as a primary DM title for agency-looking companies (client-relationship role).

smartlead_campaigns._routing: Daily run routes each lead into ONE of the 4 campaigns. STEP 1 (On-Amazon check, user-specified method 2026-05-27): Google-search '[company name] amazon' and check the results — if the brand has an Amazon storefront or product listings (e.g. amazon.com/stores/<brand>, or /dp/ product pages for their products), they ARE on Amazon -> 'Present on Amazon' pair; if no Amazon listings for the brand appear, they are NOT -> 'Not on Amazon' pair. STEP 2 (Hard/Soft A/B split): within the chosen pair, split leads ~50/50 between Hard and Soft. Each lead lands in exactly ONE campaign. STEP 0 (email gate): every lead MUST have a verified email before push (Prospeo primary; if dry, the lead goes to the LinkedIn/HeyReach fallback, not the email campaign).
smartlead_campaigns._settings: All 4 PAUSED. Each: tz America/New_York, Mon-Fri 09:00-18:00, min 20 min between emails, max 50 new leads/day, send_as_plain_text true, tracking OFF (DONT_TRACK_EMAIL_OPEN + DONT_TRACK_LINK_CLICK), stop on REPLY_TO_AN_EMAIL, follow_up_percentage 50.

theirstack_saved_search.negative_keywords_rationale: Seeded from the 25-row blurred TAM sample (2026-05-27). The bare lowercase 'amazon' title pattern is the biggest noise source (substring-matches AWS/Bedrock/logistics/agency roles) — kept because dropping it would lose good Amazon-titled roles not in the explicit list, so noise is handled via negatives instead. Four noise buckets: AWS/tech, Amazon agencies (competitors, heavy in DE), brand aggregators (E-Commerce M&A), and junior/temp. Agencies hiring clean-titled roles still slip past keyword blocks and must be caught by company name during the daily review.

Rationale: we target brands whose HQ is in NA/high-GDP Europe; a US-HQ brand posting a remote/overseas Amazon role is still a US-HQ buyer. NOTE: Bjion's original pre-built search used Job Location — overridden to HQ Location at setup. The API filter block above uses job_country_code_or as the free-test/dry-run proxy (established pattern across all TheirStack briefs).

Role.instructions: Direct field lookup WITH email-readability normalisation. Copy the Jobs row's 'Job Title' value, then normalise so it reads naturally after the hardcoded 'Saw you were hiring a ___' hook. Rules: (1) Replace ', ' separating a level word from a function area with ' of ' (e.g. 'Director, E-Commerce' -> 'Director of E-Commerce'). (2) Drop bracketed/parenthetical text and any (m/w/d) / (f/m/x) gender tags and location suffixes (e.g. 'Amazon Manager (m/w/d) — Remote DACH' -> 'Amazon Manager'). (3) If the title is in a non-English language, translate to the natural English equivalent (e.g. 'Projektmanager Amazon Marketing' -> 'Amazon Marketing Project Manager'). (4) Trim whitespace. (5) Preserve seniority words (Senior, Director, Manager, Head, VP, Lead, Chief). Only escalate to an LLM if genuinely ambiguous after rule-based normalisation.
Role.validation: Non-empty. Reads naturally after 'Saw you were hiring a ___'. No commas in the level-word/function-area position. No parens, no (m/w/d) tags, no trailing location/remote suffix. English.
